title: Heat, Moisture Loads, Dehumidification and Control Capacity

content.overview: Environmental equipment must respond to dynamic heat and moisture loads created by lighting, crop transpiration, irrigation and outside conditions. A room can hold the same thermostat setpoint while still failing moisture control, or vice versa.

vocabulary.definition: Heat load that changes air temperature.
Moisture load associated with water vapor that must be removed or condensed.
Available control capacity beyond the current operating load.

sections.title: Plants create a changing moisture load
sections.body: Transpiration varies with crop size, light, temperature, humidity, root-zone water and developmental stage. Dehumidification requirements therefore change through the crop cycle.

sections.title: Lighting contributes heat while plant response changes with temperature
sections.body: Higher air temperature can alter yield and metabolite outcomes in genotype-specific ways, so cooling capacity should be assessed as part of crop-environment management rather than only human comfort.

sections.title: Control systems can fight each other
sections.body: Cooling, reheating, humidification, dehumidification and ventilation may create inefficient loops if sequences are not coordinated. Trend data should show when systems operate and whether crop conditions actually improve.

workedExamples: If humidity rises after irrigation while temperature remains stable, the limiting problem may be latent moisture removal rather than cooling capacity.
If lights-off causes rapid cooling and RH rise, review moisture removal and temperature-control sequencing together.
commonMistakes: Sizing environmental control from empty-room conditions.
Treating humidity and temperature as independent loads.
Assuming one equipment capacity remains adequate as crop biomass increases.
content.practicalApplication: Trend room temperature, RH, irrigation events, lighting state and environmental-equipment operation over several days. Identify transitions where control loses margin or systems oppose each other.
content.summary: Advanced HVAC and dehumidification management is load management. Crop water release, lighting heat and control sequencing must be evaluated together.
